s2: A society treasurer is an unpaid volunteer who signs for the society's money. When the registrar asks for the resolution behind a payment and there is none, the volunteer who signed is answerable.
s3: Resident apps log who approved it. Society Room proves they had the right to.
s4: Same message, into Society Room. Switch refuses it before the treasurer agent sees it. Not a prompt: addressing, enforced by the platform.
s5: One template creates both rooms and four agents. The treasurer agent takes instructions from its owner only. Fifteen of fifteen addressing checks pass.
s6: Even the Treasurer is refused. No passed resolution for this invoice.
s7: The Chairman opens a meeting. The clerk takes the exclusive meeting-chair role, counts quorum, forty-one present, twenty needed, and records each vote by name. R-001 passes four to one, and the role is released.
s8: Now, and only now, the treasurer agent books it: invoice, resolution and bye-law check, all three.
s9: This is what the auditor signs. The ledger line cites the invoice and the resolution. The resolution records who voted. The bye-law sets the limit.
s10: A four-lakh repainting bid is over the limit for a society this size. The committee cannot approve it, even by vote. It goes to the General Body.
s11: In the residents' room a member asks why the lift cost sixty-eight thousand. The concierge answers only from the published records, and cites them.
s12: Switch decides who may instruct. The engine decides what is allowed. Same ledger the auditor signs.
